q: I search for version 1.5 and grep also matches 105. Which option fixes that?
expl: -F treats the pattern as plain text. Without it, the dot matches any character, so "1.5" also matches "105".

q: I search for the word log and also get login and catalog. Which option keeps only whole words?
expl: -w accepts a match only when it is a word of its own, so login and catalog are dropped.

q: Type a recursive grep for `TODO` in the current folder, with line numbers, that skips the `node_modules` and `.git` folders.
expl: --exclude-dir takes a folder name and can be repeated. Plain --exclude is for file names, so it doesn't skip folders.
You give a folder name, not a path, so grep skips node_modules wherever it is, for example web/node_modules too.
opts: Only ./node_modules at the top of the project
Every folder named node_modules, at any depth
Files named node_modules, but not folders

q: What does this print in the demo project? (dist/app.min.js has a TODO, bin/tool is a binary file with TODO in it.)
expl: -I skips the binary bin/tool, but dist was not excluded this time, so the minified file is still listed.

q: A script that runs under plain `sh` contains `grep -rnI TODO --exclude-dir={node_modules,.git,dist} .` What happens?
expl: The {a,b,c} trick is a bash feature. Plain sh passes it to grep as one odd folder name, so write the options out one by one.
opts: The same two lines as in bash
The braces are not expanded, so none of the three folders is skipped
sh stops with a syntax error

q: `grep -rnI "TODO" --exclude-dir={node_modules,.git,dist} .` prints two lines. Why can it still miss a to-do?
expl: grep matches case exactly by default. In the demo, the lowercase to-do in src/main.py only shows up with -i.
ch: Case, file types and file names
opts: -I hides text files that are too long
The search is case-sensitive, so a lowercase `# todo:` is skipped; add `-i`
grep stops after the first match in each folder

q: Type a command that prints only the names of the `.py` files under the current folder that contain `todo` in any case (TODO, todo, ...).
expl: -i ignores case, -l prints just file names, and --include="*.py" limits the search to Python files.
ch: Case, file types and file names

q: Which command finds lines with `TODO`, `FIXME` or `DEBUG` in one search?
expl: -E turns on extended patterns, where the vertical bar means "or". Without -E, the bar is just a character to find.

q: Type a command that shows the `TODO` line in `src/auth.py`, with its line number and the one line after it.
expl: -A 1 adds one line After the match. -B shows lines Before it, and -C both.
